s1.syndrome_frame: Acute right lower quadrant abdominal pain with fever and elevated inflammatory markers
salient_findings: Abdominal CT scan showing a swollen and thickened tubular structure with a pericecal collection
key_facts: 24-hour history of right iliac fossa pain
History of laparoscopic appendectomy 8 months earlier
Pain in the right lower quadrant without peritoneal signs
Abdominal CT scan showing a swollen and thickened tubular structure
Pericecal collection adjacent to surgical clips

raw.syndrome_frame: Acute right lower quadrant abdominal pain with fever and elevated inflammatory markers
salient_findings: Abdominal CT scan showing a swollen and thickened tubular structure with a pericecal collection
key_facts: 24-hour history of right iliac fossa pain
History of laparoscopic appendectomy 8 months earlier
Pain in the right lower quadrant without peritoneal signs
Abdominal CT scan showing a swollen and thickened tubular structure
Pericecal collection adjacent to surgical clips

shortlist.label: Appendiceal stump appendicitis
shortlist.why_kept: History of laparoscopic appendectomy and current right iliac fossa pain

shortlist.label: Pericecal abscess
shortlist.why_kept: Abdominal CT scan showing pericecal collection adjacent to surgical clips

shortlist.label: Cecal diverticulitis
shortlist.why_kept: Swollen and thickened tubular structure at the cecal pole on CT scan

shortlist.label: Typhlitis
shortlist.why_kept: Elevated white-blood-cell count and C-reactive protein level, consistent with typhlitis

shortlist.label: Meckel's diverticulitis
shortlist.why_kept: Right lower quadrant pain and elevated inflammatory markers, possible Meckel's diverticulum complication

raw.rationale: The patient's history of laparoscopic appendectomy 8 months earlier and the presence of a swollen and thickened tubular structure at the cecal pole with a pericecal collection adjacent to surgical clips on the abdominal CT scan support this diagnosis, as it suggests inflammation of the appendiceal stump.

rejected.label: Pericecal abscess
rejected.why: While the patient has a pericecal collection, the presence of a swollen and thickened tubular structure suggests a more specific diagnosis related to the appendiceal stump.

rejected.label: Cecal diverticulitis
rejected.why: There is no mention of a cecal diverticulum, and the location of the swollen structure at the cecal pole with adjacent surgical clips points more towards an issue with the appendiceal stump.

rejected.label: Typhlitis
rejected.why: Typhlitis typically involves the cecum and is more commonly seen in immunocompromised patients, which is not indicated in this case.

rejected.label: Meckel's diverticulitis
rejected.why: The location of the swollen structure at the cecal pole and the history of appendectomy suggest that the issue is related to the appendiceal stump rather than a Meckel's diverticulum, which is typically located in the small intestine.
